experiments.paper_location: Section 4.4, CPU/GPU attention partition and output/normalizer merge
experiments.mechanism: Execute pinned LSHSparseAttnServer.fill, plan, decode and clear AST statements using CPU surrogates, and compare partition/centering, disjoint normalized output and LSE merging with an independently enumerated FP64 union-attention oracle.

conditions.execution: Nine exact AST-selected pinned source regions; Python stdlib and previously verified restricted list-Tensor substitute. No source arithmetic changes.
conditions.seed: fixed literal key/value/query formulas; no random projections or model inputs
conditions.scope: sink/local/offloaded/new token disjointness; two requests, two KV heads, short valid sequences; dense/sparse fill copy and length state; append centering; plan increments; clear/reuse; GQA group sizes 1,4,8
conditions.oracle: Independent FP64 dot products and direct union exponent normalization; p=1 for static/new tokens, 0.4/0.65 for sampled offload, p=1 for full selection; base-2 LSE checked alongside outputs
conditions.sensitivity: Omitted sparse probability correction, inconsistent/stale centering and natural-log/base-2 LSE mixing each produce an observable numerical discrepancy
conditions.short_input_limit: seq_len <= sink + local produces an empty offload reduction in the pinned source and is explicitly unsupported here; two such negative characterization cases are not correctness passes
conditions.capacity: Host bounds assert plan length within configured page size; native capacity checks and stream/transfer ordering are unverified
conditions.adapter_arithmetic: FP64 tensor, no BF16/Torch conversion; selected cache copies are a host copy surrogate; host FlashInfer merge_state replacement computes stable base-2 weighted average
conditions.sanitizers: Python AST substitute is not an ASan/UBSan/LSan test; existing C++ suites provide separate native sanitizer evidence

experiments.note: Scoped source-behavior and CPU numerical contract, not production Torch/FlashInfer integration or native GPU scheduling. Real FBGEMM dispatch, pinning, asynchronous transfers, thread races and end-to-end model generation are unexecuted. Keep existing #65-#68 and #72-#77 repairs open; do not promote characterized invalid sizes or empty offload to production support.
